findings.title: basedOn.d253.role still claims last-heading custody, making the subject the only leftover-join in the register with two 'Last live heading at dispatch' claimants and contradicting three of its own fields
findings.subjectText: Last live heading at dispatch. Last-heading custody only.
findings.predecessorText: Last live heading at dispatch. Last-heading custody only.
evidence: The dispatch fixes the last heading as D-318, and live COORD confirms it: the final '## D-' heading in docs/coop/COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md is line 18439 '## D-318 - Record g29-fixture-corpus.v1 as DR-G29 leftover-design fixture implementations'. D-253 is therefore not the last live heading at this dispatch.

The subject already assigns that custody elsewhere: $.basedOn.d318.role opens 'Last live heading at dispatch. Last-heading custody only.', and $.basedOn.d317.role and $.basedOn.d316.role each state 'Last-heading custody remains D-318.' The d253 sentence contradicts all three.

The predecessor's sentence was true in its own mouth - at g29 leftover-join.v4's dispatch D-253 WAS the last live heading - so this is a carried string the v4-to-v5 advance missed, the same class as the g30 leftover-join.v6 Stage A SHOULD-FIX where proposedLaterWork[0] kept the superseded target while sibling fields advanced.

The lineage convention is one claimant and an explicit demotion for every other recording: within this same file $.basedOn.d229.role and $.basedOn.d204.role both carry 'Not last-heading.' The subject demotes the two older G29 recordings but not D-253.

Frozen g30-leftover-join.v7 (dual ACCEPT 0/0, dispatched at this same HEAD 3f1f11d6) shows the exact repair shape for the analogous cross-lineage entry: $.basedOn.d254.role reads 'Recorded g29 leftover-join.v4. Not last-heading. Last-heading custody remains D-318.'

Register-wide scan of all 239 *-leftover-join.v*.json artifacts for basedOn roles matching /last live heading at dispatch/i: 164 carry zero claimants, 74 carry exactly one, and g29-leftover-join.v5 is the ONLY artifact carrying two ('d318' and 'd253').

D-253 is a cross-lineage recording: git log -1 cbe471bfc0de4b49791d40c9d795b57dbb2a298c gives 'D-253: record g28 leftover-join.v4'. So the second last-heading claimant in a G29 artifact is another lineage's leftover-join recording, which is the dispatched attack 'last-heading custody carrying leftover-join lineage of another lineage'.
findings.whyMustFix: Last-heading custody is the fact that fixes which COORD heading the candidate was measured against, and it is the one custody claim a later D-000 recording relies on when pinning the artifact. This is not a dropped assertion redundantly bound elsewhere - it is an affirmatively false proposition asserted in the record, and it collides with the correct claim in the same object. A reader auditing custody finds two mutually exclusive claimants and cannot resolve which heading governs from the bytes. It also lands a named dispatch attack squarely, which is the factor that separates this from the SHOULD-FIX calibration used where a misattributed disclaimer is separately asserted at speaker level and no dispatch attack succeeds through the gap.
findings.repairShape: Rewrite $.basedOn.d253.role so it demotes D-253 and names what it recorded, in the frozen g30 leftover-join.v7 $.basedOn.d254.role shape: 'Recorded g28 leftover-join.v4. Not last-heading. Last-heading custody remains D-318. g29 leftover-join.v5 does not remasure G28.' Leave $.basedOn.d318.role as the sole last-heading claimant. No other field needs to move; the subject's head, recordedInputs.HEAD and D-318 custody statements are already correct.

decision.rule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. One MUST-FIX stands, so the verdict is REJECT.
decision.scope: This review measures g29-leftover-join.v5 as a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED leftover-design remasurement that binds NOTHING. It does not SATISFY DR-117, DR-131 or DR-133, does not close leftover-design of OBL-G29-FX-AUTHORING, and records no recording act. All custody digests, the ten-fixture ground truth and the singleton leftover-design residual hold. Twenty-three of twenty-five attacks are fully refuted; the two that are not (A09, A20) both trace to a single defect, the carried last-heading custody sentence at $.basedOn.d253.role.
